the goldfish radial glial transcriptome is enriched in neuroactive and immunomodulatory factors, and that secretoneurin regulates transcriptional networks involved in neurogenesis and immune function.
the transcriptome of goldfish RGC is highly enriched with genes related to the CNS and immune system, and that SNa is a potent regulator of RGC gene expression.

the first transcriptome for fish radial glial cells (the most abundant glia in the fish brain) reveals a diverse repertoire of genes that may respond to and regulate an array of hormones/peptides, and that a secretogranin-derived neuropeptide, secretoneurin, modulates transcriptional networks related to neurogenesis and immune function in these cells.

identifying novel functions of the neuropeptide SNa and the mechanisms by which SNa regulates neurogenesis and immune functions.

the RGC transcriptome is highly responsive to SNa and that SNa is a potent regulator of neurogenesis and immune responses in fish RGCs.
